item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (July 26)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Oman-Iran talks advance on reopening Strait of Hormuz, sources say
item.description: Talks between Oman and Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and their respective territorial waterways have made progress, two sources told CBS News.

item.title: Sen. Bernie Sanders calls for negotiated end to Iran war and talks 2026 midterms
item.description: Independent Sen. Bernie Sanders shared his thoughts on the upcoming midterm elections, including how he thinks progressive candidates may fare, on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan." He also called for a negotiated end to the war in Iran.

item.title: Open: This is "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," July 26, 2026
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Sens. Bernie Sanders and John Kennedy discuss the war with Iran and the 2026 midterm elections. U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz and former FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb also join, and CBS News director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto shares the latest CBS News poll results.

item.title: Home, not alone: Helping aging seniors in rural America
item.description: Health risks associated with loneliness and social isolation are more common among the aging population of rural America. In North Dakota, the program Aging in Community aims to build connections among neighbors to help isolated rural seniors.

item.title: Nature: Great white sharks in Mexico
item.description: We leave you this Sunday swimming with sharks off the coast of Guadalupe Island in Mexico. Videographer: Maurico Handler.

item.title: How plants feel
item.description: Science shows us that, even though plants don't have brains, they seem to have a nervous system that responds to touch in remarkable ways. Robert Krulwich and puppeteer Barnaby Dixon explore the science of thigmomorphogenesis (the phenomenon of plants reacting to outside stimulae), a discussion that plants the seeds for a song.

item.title: The adventurous life of supermodel Lauren Hutton
item.description: She didn't set out to be a model, or an actress, and several agencies rejected the gap-toothed Lauren Hutton, before Eileen Ford gave her a shot. As the face of Revlon, Hutton became the highest-paid model in history, and still holds the record for most cover appearances on American Vogue. She talks with Anthony Mason about her adventurous life of no regrets – from living among the bushmen of the Kalahari, to a near-fatal motorcycle accident in 2000. Even of the low points she says, "I'd do it again in a second." (Originally broadcast Jan. 25, 2026.)

item.title: The "magic" of worm grunting
item.description: If you are looking for live fishing bait, you could dig up some worms – or, you could use a bizarre trick involving vibrations to conjure earthworms out of the soil. Correspondent Conor Knighton looks into a little-understood process known as "worm grunting." He also visits Sopchoppy, Florida, the self-described "Worm Capital of the World," to attend the Worm Gruntin' Festival – a big party celebrating the town's favorite invertebrate. (Originally aired June 15, 2025.)

item.title: 7/26: New York Times bestseller lists
item.description: Check out this week's top-selling titles on The New York Times fiction and non-fiction lists.

item.title: These United States: Revolutionary War hero Thaddeus Kosciuszko
item.description: Polish-born Thaddeus Kosciuszko (1746-1817) was a military engineer who became key to Gen. George Washington's success against the British. Mo Rocca looks at the immigrant hero whose contributions to the Revolutionary War helped secure independence for America.

item.title: More than 300,000 displaced in France and Spain as wildfires rage
item.description: Forests in Spain and France have been parched by successive heatwaves since May that have brought drought to many areas.

item.title: Passage: Late-night TV exec Peter Lassally
item.description: During his half-century in television, Peter Lassally (who died last Sunday at age 93) played producer and confidant to late-night hosts David Letterman, Craig Ferguson, Tom Snyder, and Johnny Carson. Mo Rocca has a remembrance of the man they called "The Host Whisperer."

item.title: Corinne Bailey Rae on the sadness of loss and the beauty of life
item.description: Twenty years after her single "Put Your Records On" made her an international star, the two-time Grammy-winner is embarking on a tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of her breakout debut album.

item.title: Extended interview: Corinne Bailey Rae
item.description: In this web exclusive, British singer-songwriter Corinne Bailey Rae talks with Seth Doane about growing up in Leeds and feeling on the margins; the influence of Billie Holiday and Kurt Cobain on her music; the breakout success of "Put Your Records On"; the devastating loss of her first husband; finding love again; and what aging has taught her.

item.title: A Summer Song: Corinne Bailey Rae
item.description: Twenty years after her single "Put Your Records On" made her an international star, two-time Grammy-winner Corinne Bailey Rae is embarking on a tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of her breakout debut album. The British singer-songwriter talks with correspondent Seth Doane about the inspiration of Billie Holiday and Kurt Cobain; grieving the death of her first husband; and of rebirth – a life after loss.

item.title: Artist Derrick Adams' depictions of Black joy
item.description: At 56, Derrick Adams is widely regarded as one of the most important artists of his generation, known for capturing the Black experience in vibrant, kaleidoscopic colors.

item.title: Artist Derrick Adams' depictions of Black joy
item.description: At 56, Derrick Adams is widely regarded as one of the most important artists of his generation, known for capturing the Black experience in vibrant, kaleidoscopic colors. Correspondent Nancy Giles talks with the artist about leaving his mark with his depictions of joyous scenes of everyday life. She also visits the Institute of Contemporary Art in Boston, home to a mid-career retrospective of Adams' art.

item.title: How Trump admin cuts have compromised food safety
item.description: Since May, more than 11,000 cases of illness caused by the parasite cyclospora have been reported in 41 states. This comes after the Trump administration drastically cut FDA and CDC staff, prompting one expert to call this summer's outbreaks "a national wake-up call."

item.title: How Trump admin cuts have compromised food safety
item.description: Since May, more than 11,000 cases of cyclosporiasis, caused by a parasite, have been reported in 41 states. The outbreak comes after the Trump administration drastically cut FDA and CDC staff; disbanded a national advisory committee on how to prevent microbial contamination in food; winnowed down an early-warning surveillance program for specific pathogens; and further delayed a rule that would have required tracing contaminants from field to store. Correspondent David Pogue talks with experts who see the current compromises of food safety as "a national wake-up call."

item.title: ICE to target Haitians as Temporary Protected Status is set to end, sources say
item.description: The plans include arresting migrants in Ohio and quickly putting them on deportation flights to crisis-stricken Haiti, the internal documents indicate.

item.title: Berlin ramming attack believed to be act of Islamist extremist terror, officials say
item.description: German police have identified the suspect as 21-year-old Abdul B. and warned the public that he may be armed and dangerous.

item.title: Almanac: July 26
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.

item.title: Love thy neighbor: Helping aging seniors in the heartland
item.description: According to the USDA, the number of counties where at least 20% of residents are over the age of 65 has nearly tripled since 2010 – and it's in those older, more rural populations where the health risks associated with loneliness and social isolation are more common. Correspondent Lee Cowan goes to North Dakota, where the program Aging in Community, aimed at building connections among neighbors, takes a grassroots approach to helping rural seniors.

item.title: 7/26: Sunday Morning
item.description: Hosted by Mo Rocca. Featured: Aging in rural America; compromises to food safety; supermodel and actress Lauren Hutton; singer Corinne Bailey Rae; artist Derrick Adams; worm grunting; and how plants are affected by touch.

item.title: Suspect in Berlin LGBTQ+ parade attack has ties to Islamic "circles," police say
item.description: Berlin police did not identify the suspect, who is still at large, by name but said that he was already known to police and is from Berlin.

item.title: Cyclospora outbreak dubbed "lettuce-gate" as health concerns spread across U.S.
item.description: Americans say they aren't convinced the cyclospora outbreak is under control as confirmed cases near 2,000.

item.title: India education minister resigns after weeks of "Cockroach" protests
item.description: Movement organizers said the government had accepted their remaining demands and called off future protests.

item.title: ChatGPT now has a space for sharing medical records. Should you?
item.description: OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.

item.title: SpaceX's Super Heavy-Starship blasts off on 13th test flight
item.description: An upgraded version of the world's most powerful rocket is key to landing NASA astronauts on the moon in the agency's Artemis program.
